blocks.h2: Why Does Sewer Line Maintenance Matter?
blocks.intro: Sewer line maintenance catches problems while they're still small and prevents them from becoming expensive fixes down the line. Here's what regular checkups can do for you:

tiles.body: Roots are caught before they turn into a blockage.
An aging or clay pipe gets flagged before it cracks.
A minor slow drain doesn't get the chance to turn into a full backup.
A small fix doesn't turn into a big one.

blocks.h2: How Often Does a Highland Park Sewer Line Need Maintenance?
blocks.intro: How often your line needs a checkup depends mostly on your pipe's age and what's growing near it. Nearly half of Highland Park homes were built before 1960, and many sit on lots with mature trees, so most homes here land in the first two rows.
head: Risk Tier
Recommended Frequency
Why
rows: Older homes (clay, cast iron, or other aging pipe)
These materials are more prone to cracking, shifting, and joint failure, especially as they age
Tree roots are the leading cause of sewer line blockages and work into small cracks over time
Newer homes (PVC or modern plastic pipe)
These materials resist roots and corrosion better, so less frequent checks are usually enough
blocks.note: Not sure which category fits your home? A first inspection tells us exactly where you stand.

blocks.h2: Sewer Maintenance for Highland Park Homes
blocks.intro: Two facts make regular checkups worth it here: the line is yours, and the trees are big.

items.h3: You Own the Line to the Main
items.body: In Highland Park, the homeowner owns and maintains the private sewer line from the house to the city main. The city's flood tips recommend having it checked for roots and debris. A maintenance visit is that check.
Highland Park's ravines and tree-lined streets put a lot of roots near older clay pipe. Catching early growth on camera costs far less than a backup in a finished basement.

blocks.h2: What a Maintenance Visit Can (and Can't) Fix
blocks.intro: A maintenance visit is built around prevention, not repair. Here's where the line falls:
head: Included in a Maintenance Visit
Needs a Different Service
rows: A camera inspection to check your line's current condition
An active sewage backup. Likely fix: [Emergency Plumbing](/highland-park/emergency-plumbing)
Catching early root growth or wear before it becomes a bigger problem
A cracked or collapsed pipe. Likely fix: [Sewer Repair](/highland-park/sewer-repair)
A light interior clean as part of the visit
A heavy clog that needs full clearing. Likely fix: [Sewer Rodding](/highland-park/sewer-rodding) or [Hydro Jetting](/highland-park/hydro-jetting)
An honest assessment of what your line needs next
A line at the end of its lifespan. Likely fix: [Trenchless Sewer Repair](/highland-park/trenchless-sewer-repair)
blocks.note: If your line needs more than a checkup, we'll tell you exactly what and why. No surprise upsells.

blocks.intro: A maintenance visit stays a maintenance visit, not a sales pitch for something bigger.

steps.body: We run a camera down your line at every visit. You see the same footage we do, so you know your line's actual condition, not a guess.
We'll tell you straight if everything looks good, or if something's starting to develop. We don't manufacture urgency to sell a bigger job.
Once we know what your line needs, you get a flat rate before anything starts.

blocks.h2: Sewer Maintenance Questions From Highland Park Homeowners

items.q: How often should a Highland Park sewer line be maintained?
items.preview: Older clay or cast iron lines: once a year. Mature trees nearby: every one to two years.
items.answer: It depends on your pipe's age and what's around it. Older pipes, like clay or cast iron, benefit from a check at least once a year. Homes with mature trees nearby should aim for every one to two years. With nearly half of Highland Park homes built before 1960, most lines here fall into one of those two groups.

items.q: What does a sewer maintenance visit include?
items.preview: A camera inspection, an honest read on your line and a light interior clean.
items.answer: A maintenance visit starts with a [camera inspection](/highland-park/video-camera-sewer-inspections) to check your line's current condition. From there, we give you an honest read on what we see, along with a light interior clean as part of the visit. If something bigger turns up, we'll walk you through it before recommending any next steps.

items.q: Does regular maintenance actually prevent expensive repairs?
items.preview: Most sewer emergencies give early warning signs. Maintenance catches them while the fix is small.
items.answer: Sewer line emergencies are some of the most expensive plumbing problems a homeowner can face, and most of them don't happen without warning. Regular maintenance catches early signs, like root growth or a developing crack, while they're still a small, inexpensive fix.

items.q: What's the difference between maintenance and repair?
items.preview: Maintenance is preventive. Repair is for an actual crack, break or backup.
items.answer: Maintenance is scheduled and preventive: a camera inspection and light upkeep to catch problems early. Repair is what happens once there's an actual issue, like a crack, a break, or a line that's already backing up. If your maintenance visit turns up something more serious, that's when [a repair conversation](/highland-park/sewer-repair) starts.
